column1: # Expected bindings rows for the bindings trap fixture (python).
# one per line, byte-sorted. scripts/check.sh asserts this set exactly against
# <out>/bindings.tsv: a missing line is a binding the extractor stopped finding,
# an extra line is one it invented. Both are regressions.
# Written from the fixture sources and the bindings spec alone, by an
# independent oracle that never saw the extractor or its output; the two are
# reconciled separately. `to` is pinned to the edges in EXPECTED.tsv.
# Regenerate deliberately, never reflexively - the point of the file is
# that it does not move when the extractor changes.
# - from-import of a submodule gives one row per name, kind module, to the submodule file; the M edge (app/models/__init__.py) EXPECTED.tsv also lists gets no row.

# - app/models/thing.py:6 from . import thing, base: thing resolves as a submodule to the importing file itself, which has no edge, so the row is module with empty to/conf (not a named row to app/models/__init__.py); base is an ordinary module row.

# - app/main.py:5 and app/reports.py:5 parenthesised lists (opened mid-line / continued on line 6): every row carries the from line 5; `database as db` -> db, `base as baseline` -> baseline, imported * (module kind).

# - app/loader.py is CRLF: the CR is not part of any name and adds no line; `import os; from app.models import database, \` gives os plus database/base, all on line 5; `import app.util, \` gives app.util and app.util.base on line 8.

# - app/continuations.py:7-8 `import app.models, \` + `app.util; import app.reports`: app.models and app.util carry line 7 (their statement's start); import app.reports starts on physical line 8, so its row carries line 8, not the logical line's 7.
# - app/continuations.py:13 import app.util after `x = 1 + \` / `2` / `# note` is its own statement on line 13 (a second app.util row, distinct by line).

# - app/help_text.py:6 "; from app import (x" inside a string is data: no row; :8 from app import util -> util is a subpackage (app/util/__init__.py), module row with module column `app`; the M edge to app/__init__.py (undotted `app`, exact root match) gets no row.

# - app/backslash_variants.py:7-9 `from app import models, \` + `util; from app.other import reports, \` + `d`: models/util carry line 7, module app; the second statement starts on physical line 8 and gets its own module app.other (reports/d are names in app/other.py, not submodules: named rows).
# - app/backslash_variants.py:11-12 the trailing backslash inside the parentheses is only a continuation (no name `\`): models/util module rows on line 11.
# - app/paren_then_stmt.py:5-6 `import app.reports` after `util);` on line 6 is its own statement on line 6, not part of the from-list (line 5).
# - app/string_continuation.py:5-6 "a; \<newline>import app.evil" is one string: no row, no edge to app/evil.py; `import app.util` after the closing quote and `;` starts on line 6.
# - from app import ... (undotted M, exact root match to app/__init__.py): the M edge gets no row, as for every from-import.
# - app/registry.py:5 `as b` binds the first element only: b (module app.models.base) and app.models.thing (dotted local as written).
# - Bare undotted os, a_package_not_in_this_tree (module rows) and a_missing_reporting_lib (named row build_chart): no root-level (or src/) file of that name, so empty to/conf.
# - conf is each statement's own resolution; every Python resolution here is an exact package path, EXTRACTED.
